summary: Conservative opt-tuning safety net: tenant sees intermittent 5xx and elevated tail latency after enabling kv-prefetch + q4 quant profile
description:
Issue summary: After enabling a tenant-level optimizer profile that enables aggressive KV prefetch (window=32) and a 4-bit quant profile (q4_mixed) the customer reports intermittent 5xx errors and a noticeable P99 tail latency increase for interactive chat routes.

Impact: Intermittent 5xx responses (approx 0.6% of requests during peak) and P95->P99 jump from ~450ms to ~1.2s for the tenant's primary chat route. Customer reports visible user complaints and warned they may revert to a competitor if unresolved.

Environment: Dedicated pool in prod-us-east serving BrightPost Health tenant. Traffic is primarily short-turn chat (avg seq len 80 tokens). The change was applied during a low-traffic maintenance window two days ago and rolled to 100% tenant traffic 90 minutes after initial canary.

Observed behavior: 1) Spikes of 502/503 with upstream serving-runtime logs showing 'KV_CACHE_MISS' thrashing followed by 'INFERENCE_TIMEOUT' entries. 2) Node-level GPU memory pressure observed on 2/6 nodes in the tenant pool with ephemeral OOM logs during the same window. 3) Error rate correlates with a rise in 'async_batch_queue_time' metric and increased packet-drop on egress links.

Expected behavior: Stable error rate (<=0.01%) and tail latencies within baseline SLO (P95 < 500ms, P99 < 800ms).

Attachments: telemetry snippets, trace ids, and sample request/response pairs included in logs field below.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Apply optimizer profile: kv_prefetch.window=32, enable async_batching=true, quant_profile=q4_mixed on tenant.
2) Route steady chat traffic that matches customer's seq length distribution (avg 80 tokens, 95th 330 tokens).
3) Observe tail latency and error rates over 30 minutes.
4) Check serving-runtime logs for KV eviction/rehydration patterns and scheduler for batch queue buildup.
logs: Sample traces: trace-id: bp-20260309-1a2b (P99 1.32s, 503). Serving logs: 'kv_cache: eviction_count=456, prefetch_errors=12', 'scheduler: async_batch_wait_ms=1200', 'gpu0: mem_used=33000MiB / 34000MiB', recent Kubernetes pod events show transient OOMKilled on node-tn-04. Full log bundle uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/bpprod/sup-836201/log-bundle.tar.gz
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: aggressive kv_prefetch expanded resident KV working set combined with q4_mixed memory layout caused increased GPU memory pressure and cache thrash, leading to longer queue times and timeouts. Alternate hypothesis: async batching combined with variable sequence lengths produced long-tail batching delays.

What we checked: recent rollout timeline, per-host GPU metrics, KV cache hit ratios, async batch queue histograms, tenant-specific traffic split. No code changes to serving runtime at rollout time besides optimizer config toggles. No infra events in cluster except the OOMs on two nodes pinned to tenant pool.

Immediate actions taken: 1) Scoped traffic split: we reduced the tenant rollout from 100% to 50% on the original snapshot to reduce pressure. 2) Created short-term circuit: lowered kv_prefetch.window to 8 for the tenant as a canary. 3) Temporarily pinned tenant to q8 quant profile for 30 minutes during the investigation which brought P99 back to ~780ms and reduced 5xxs to ~0.05%.

Next investigative steps: correlate per-request KV size distribution, run a tenant replay in staging with identical seq distribution, and test progressive kv_prefetch window sizing to identify inflection point.

2026-03-09 - SRE (Diego Morales): Performed quick gating: rolled traffic back to snapshot-2026-0309-09 for tenant and temporarily set kv_prefetch.window=8. Observed immediate drop in 5xx. Requesting confirmation from customer on user-visible impact.

2026-03-10 - Customer (BrightPost SE - Maya Patel): Confirmed reduced errors after kv_prefetch window change and quant pin to q8. Reports slightly higher per-token cost but acceptable for now. Asks for recommended long-term safe rollout pattern so they can re-enable q4 in the future.

2026-03-11 - Support (Ava Chen): Proposed conservative staged rollout: (1) q8 -> shadow q4 traffic with 5% sampled traffic; (2) incremental kv_prefetch window increases 8->16->24 with 1-hour observation windows and automatic rollback on P99 or 5xx thresholds; (3) enable async_batching only after prefetched KV working set is stable. Suggested adding a circuit breaker that auto-demotes quant when per-node GPU mem_used > 90%.

2026-03-12 - SRE (Diego Morales): Implemented a tenant gating rule and created a safe rollback runbook (link in related_confluence_pages). Scheduling a staged replay in staging on 2026-03-13 to verify thresholds and collect exact inflection points for kv_prefetch window size.
suggested_workarounds:
Short term: Pin tenant to q8 quant profile and reduce kv_prefetch.window to 8, or temporarily disable kv_prefetch if memory pressure persists. Use traffic split to move 30-50% of traffic back to a known-good snapshot.

Medium term: Run a shadow q4 profile with sampled traffic and compare memory + latency metrics. Introduce an auto-demote policy that switches to q8 when GPU memory utilization >85% or P99 latency > 1s for more than 5 minutes.

Commands / config snippets (operator):
- rctl tenant update --id brightpost --optimizer kv_prefetch.window=8 --quant-profile=q8
- rctl traffic split --tenant brightpost --target-snapshot snapshot-2026-0309-09 --percent 40
- monitor: alerts for tenant.bp.p99_latency > 1s OR tenant.bp.5xx_rate > 0.2%
resolution: In progress: temporary mitigations applied (kv_prefetch.window reduced and quant pinned to q8). Customer confirmed reduced UX impact.
